content.comment_body: Hello, I'm encountering issues with my temperature sensor. The sensor operates over a 0-10V range, covering temperatures from -50 to 50°C. When I try to display the temperature on my [product_name], all I see are values around 700 instead of readable temperature numbers. I am using [product_name] and don't have much experience with it yet. Thank you!

If you check only the analog input, you'll see raw converted values. You need to use an analog amplifier block after the analog input to normalize the readings. Here are suggested settings for the analog amplifier: Sensor: 0-10V, Minimum: -500, Maximum: 500, Gain: 1.0, Offset: -500, Decimal: 1. Adding the analog amplifier will show the temperature as a decimal value in your display.

Thanks for your help, [user_name]! Could you explain how to configure the >Message Texts< block? I can't see the text displayed on [product_name] even though I followed your instructions. The B001 block is visible, but B002 is not.
Please review the attached file for guidance.

analysis.insight_summary: Users often find it challenging to interpret sensor data directly from analog inputs in [product_name] systems. The main confusion occurs when sensor values aren't automatically shown in a human-readable format, such as temperature, which results in incorrect and unclear display numbers. The lack of straightforward, beginner-level instructions in [product_name] software further complicates setting up and viewing sensor data correctly.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the temperature sensor readings to be displayed directly as clear temperature values (in °C) on the [product_name] screen, without needing to manually convert or reconfigure settings.
